page: Hetzner Cloud cpx22 is an entry-level virtual server powered by the QEMU hypervisor. It features 2 shared vCPUs based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC processor architecture running at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 4.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 1.95 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled with 80 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. The instance does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The server demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench multi-core scores, and Passmark CPU scores fall into the bottom 25%, reflecting the shared nature of the vCPUs. Memory bandwidth for large blocks and single-threaded gzip compression perform at average levels, while static web serving throughput is poor, ranking in the bottom 10%. Small-model LLM inference achieves average speeds of 498.54 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 141.46 tokens/sec for text generation using a 135M model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the cpx22 offers a budget-friendly resource profile with fast NVMe storage, though it is constrained by shared CPU allocation and limited memory. It is best suited for lightweight, non-resource-intensive workloads such as basic text processing, single-threaded scripting, small-scale development environments, or low-traffic utility services that do not require sustained multi-core performance or high memory bandwidth.
